paragraphs: North Somerset Council's fostering team is based in Weston-super-Mare and looks after children from the town, Clevedon and the rest of the district. Independent agencies such as the services shown above also care for children from the area. The council has said its greatest need is for carers who can look after children aged 11 and over, and for brothers and sisters who need to stay together.

Its stated entry requirement is simple: be over 21 and have a spare room. The council welcomes applicants of any background, age, gender, ethnicity, relationship status or sexual orientation. It describes itself as a not-for-profit service whose investment goes back into fostering, with training and support arranged locally, and it says approved carers living in North Somerset no longer pay council tax and receive increased fostering payments. Its full allowances and fees are published on the council's website, along with a financial calculator.

Enquiries now go through Fostering South West, a regional hub set up by 14 councils in the south west and funded by the Department for Education, which passes your details to the North Somerset team. From there the steps are an initial chat, a registration of interest form, a home visit, a formal application with references and checks, Skills to Foster training, an assessment over a number of weeks and the North Somerset Fostering Panel. The council says this can take up to six months; experienced carers transferring from another service can expect three to four.
Speak to the council and to two or three of the agencies above before you decide, and ask what each would offer for the age group you have in mind.
